It's not just about capital—it's about foresight, precision, and execution.I believe that leadership in finance is about creating a culture of excellence while maintaining humanity. As the Managing Director of Legend Investments, I oversee a team of 180 professionals across our investment, research, and operations divisions. My leadership philosophy centers on three pillars: empowerment, accountability, and continuous growth. I've found that the best ideas often come from the most unexpected places, so I maintain an open-door policy and encourage even our most junior analysts to challenge conventional thinking. Every Monday, I host a 'strategic roundtable' where team members from all levels can present investment theses or operational improvements. Last month, a second-year analyst proposed a novel approach to ESG scoring that we're now implementing across our portfolio. Leadership isn't about having all the answers—it's about fostering an environment where great ideas can flourish.I believe that managing wealth is a discipline that requires a long-term approach, balancing high-risk opportunities with stable, income-generating investments. My personal portfolio is a mix of equities, private equity, bonds, real estate, and alternative assets. I don't chase trends; instead, I look for opportunities with a significant margin of safety or a compelling growth narrative. The goal is not just wealth accumulation but also capital preservation and strategic growth.I believe that building a strong network is crucial in the financial industry. It's not just about having a list of contacts, but about cultivating meaningful relationships that can provide valuable insights and support. My relationship with Sarah Chen, CEO of Pacific Dynamics, is a great example of this. We met at a conference in 2008, but it was a conversation on a delayed flight from Hong Kong six months later that really solidified our connection. We talked about market trends, our shared love of jazz, and other topics, and that foundation has lasted for fifteen years. Now, she's not just a business contact, but someone I can call at 3 AM if I need a straight answer about Asian markets. That's the kind of network that makes a difference in this industry.I believe that finding a balance between work and family life is crucial for success in finance. My wife has been a constant source of support and encouragement, reminding me that time is the one asset that can't be compounded. She's also been instrumental in helping me prioritize my family and maintain a healthy work-life balance. By being present and engaged with my kids, I've been able to create lasting memories and nurture the relationships that truly matter.I believe that technology is a key driver of innovation in finance. By leveraging tools like Bloomberg Terminal and developing custom algorithms, I can stay ahead of the curve and make informed decisions. The 'Mission Control' layout I've created on my terminal is a testament to the importance of having real-time market data and tailored analysis at my fingertips. It's not just about reacting to market events, but about anticipating them. The early warning I received during the 2022 banking crisis about unusual patterns in regional bank trading volumes allowed us to adjust our positions before the market opened. The LIVE function on Bloomberg Terminal has been instrumental in facilitating seamless communication with our Asian offices during their trading hours. Technology is truly the backbone of modern finance.I believe that success is a combination of discipline, adaptability, and relationships. Discipline helps you stay consistent and put in the work required to achieve your goals. Adaptability allows you to adjust to changing circumstances and stay relevant in a rapidly evolving environment. And relationships play a crucial role in shaping your trajectory and opening doors to new opportunities. By surrounding yourself with supportive mentors, colleagues, clients, and even competitors, you can leverage their expertise and networks to achieve greater heights.
